title: Capella vs WGU: control, tuition, size
summary: Capella University (Capella) versus Western Governors University (WGU). Also searched as WGU vs Capella. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Capella University and Western Governors University (Capella vs WGU) differ primarily in ownership, enrollment, tuition, and location. Capella University is a private for-profit institution based in Minneapolis, with an undergraduate enrollment of 18,364 students and an in-state tuition of $14,400. In contrast, Western Governors University is a private nonprofit university located in Salt Lake City, serving a significantly larger undergraduate population of 155,088 students and charging a lower in-state tuition of $8,658. These distinctions highlight differences in institutional structure and scale between Capella vs WGU.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing cost, Capella University and Western Governors University (Capella vs WGU) show notable differences in tuition and student debt. Capella charges both in-state and out-of-state students $14,400 annually, whereas Western Governors University has a lower tuition rate of $8,658 for all students regardless of residency. Additionally, the median debt for students completing their programs at Capella is $14,968, which is higher than the $11,116 median debt reported by graduates of Western Governors University. These financial factors are important considerations for prospective students evaluating Capella vs WGU.
